Il carcinoma papillare (10-15% dei carci:
Papillary carcinoma (10-15% of renal carcinomas) is typically T2 hypointense, homogeneous, hypovascular: in the arterial phase it enhances little (much less than the cortex) and slowly, with progressive increase in the late phases. It may contain hemosiderin (very dark on T2 and on opposed-phase/in-phase with signal drop on the longer echo). Subtractions help demonstrate the weak enhancement, which distinguishes it from a hyperdense/hemorrhagic cyst.
Comparison: clear cell = T2 hyperintense, intense and heterogeneous arterial enhancement; chromophobe = intermediate enhancement, sometimes a central scar; lipid-poor angiomyolipoma = markedly T2 hypointense with marked arterial enhancement.
The histologic type matters for prognosis and therapy: papillary is generally less aggressive and does not respond like clear cell to anti-angiogenic therapies.
This case is useful because the T2 is atypical: papillary carcinoma can be T2 hyperintense when it has cystic, necrotic or hemorrhagic components. Low, progressive enhancement remains the most useful sign.
Per l'istotipo del carcinoma renale cont: For the histotype of renal carcinoma, what matters most is how much it enhances in the arterial phase relative to the cortex.
